title: L Is Too Big, XL Fits
surface: A woman tries a dress labeled L and finds it too large. The assistant brings the same style labeled XL, which fits perfectly. Neither dress has been altered and neither label is wrong. Why?
solution: The Roman-themed shop uses Roman numerals for its numeric sizes, not the usual letter-size abbreviations. L means 50 and XL means 40. The second dress is therefore smaller, not extra-large.

facts.text: The labels are Roman numerals, not ordinary letter-size abbreviations.
L is 50 and XL is 40, so the XL-labeled dress is smaller.
Both dresses share the same style and numeric sizing system; both labels are correct.

unknowns: The shop name, country and other sizes are unspecified.
hints: Must a letter-shaped label abbreviate an English word?
These symbols also appear on traditional clock faces.
Read Roman numerals: L is 50, XL is 40.
